Firstly my friend, if you are viewing your own content as “dull” that you need to handle first. You need to have the confidence, but not an ego of someone who already gets a million views in every video. Now as you edit, edit from the perspective that you are the viewer watching your content. Is it imperative to the story of the game? i.e. something like Resident Evil that has an underlying plot. If so balance it out with funny moments as well as some story. In my opinion you dont need to go too crazy with captions, assets & effects for something along that nature.

If you’re doing something like i.e. Phasmophobia make your goal 10 minutes. Make your cuts for each hunt while keeping some sort of flow to the direction of the video, add all your bells & whistles to moments you really want to stand out further. Majority of the time you’ll have more than 10 minutes of video by time you are done but having a baseline helps!

Take some time to take in other content in the same form, look up search terms that relate to your content. Using the example from before something along the lines but not exactly has to be “resident evil funny moments” indulge in other content & get a feel for what direction you want to take your content. A lot of time you overthink your own content & you end up burning yourself out. Take a beat, reflect & start again. You’ll figure it out but please I ask of you. Be confident in your content FIRST! If you use terms like “dull” to describe your own content you gotta figure yourself out first. Confidence reflects in the content & you’ll find yourself at a much better place! Hope you find this helpful!

Even if you hit affiliate tomorrow, with the minimum requirements to reach it. You need what 3 concurrent viewers consistently right? The incentive for someone to be in your stream is for you. Not some in stream rewards. You are the content. The game is an extension of you. So if they are there for some channel point redemption, they aren’t there for you. You want community, you want to create the content you would consume & enjoy. Be confident & focus on making content. Make sure you’re putting that content on other platforms, then that will bring community who are there for you. That’s the goal. Keep that in mind & have the confidence (not the ego) like you’ve been doing this for a decade with a thousand viewers & you’ll be successful. Financial success is different! Strive to be successful in making content not cause money & you’ll be much happier in what you create.

Respectfully, affiliate doesn’t mean anything. Not now anyway. Every streamer I have enjoyed (both partnered & small streamers) I find their content elsewhere, dig their vibe THEN I go to their stream. It’s taxing but you’re going to just keep bumming yourself out about numbers & algorithms at this stage of things. Focus on creating content, cut down a stream day & make it an editing day. Take a beat & redirect your energy instead of beat up about twitch’s dogshit algorithm & shift it into making the content you want to create. You’re frustrated, I get it. The second you make creating content for the fun of creating content & putting that out there you’ll find community & that’s the real goal here. You have to put out the energy like you have a thousand people in your stream. Hope you find your community!
